biography: Frank Yu, a Hong Kong native, discovered his passion for speed early, navigating the bustling city streets on a modified scooter before he even hit his teens. His formal racing journey began at 18, entering local karting competitions and quickly dominating the scene with his raw talent and fearless overtaking maneuvers. A pivotal moment came during the Macau Karting Grand Prix, where despite a mechanical failure in the final lap, his aggressive driving and never-give-up attitude caught the eye of a BMW talent scout. This led to a sponsored drive in the Asian Touring Car Championship. Now at his peak, Frank races for the BMW team and aims to conquer the GT world, blending his street smarts with refined racing techniques, making him a force to be reckoned with on any track.
drivingStyle: Yu's driving style is characterized by an unwavering commitment to attack. He's known for his late-braking overtakes, often pushing the limits of adhesion to gain an advantage. While his aggression sometimes leads to minor errors, his tire management is surprisingly adept, carefully balancing early pace with longevity. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances in high-stakes situations, proving his mettle as a true racer.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision in the 2021 Asian Touring Car Championship final race, where Yu's aggressive move forced Tanaka off the track, costing him the championship.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 Bathurst 12 Hour race with a last-lap overtake, securing a historic victory for the BMW team and cementing his status as a rising star in endurance racing.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 2020 Macau Grand Prix while leading, a devastating blow in front of his home crowd that temporarily shook his confidence.
